Dq ≈ 1318 cm⁻¹, which is Δo ≈ 13 180 cm⁻¹. This is the crossing of the ⁵T₂g (high-spin) and ¹A₁g (low-spin) ground states for B = 803 cm⁻¹ and C = 3078 cm⁻¹.

I got this by numerical full-configuration calculation, not from a closed formula. I built all d⁶ Slater determinants with M_S = 0. The Coulomb repulsion used F² = 49B + 7C and F⁴ = 63C/5. I added an octahedral field of +6Dq on e_g and −4Dq on t₂g. I then split the basis by total spin (S = 0 and S = 2) and found the Dq where the lowest S = 2 energy equals the lowest S = 0 energy.

The ¹A₁g mixing with the e⁴t₂² configuration is included, because the full d⁶ basis is used.

The difference E(S=2) − E(S=0) changes sign between Dq = 1000 and 1500 cm⁻¹:

| Dq (cm⁻¹) | E(S=2) − E(S=0) (cm⁻¹) |
|---|---|
| 1000 | −6078 |
| 1500 | +3517 |
| 2000 | +13231 |

The root is at Dq ≈ 1318 cm⁻¹.
